subject: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC - ops playbook & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Laura Gomez <laura@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: deployment isolation needs

Hi Laura — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a clean canary and SOW: 

- Your primary requirement: processing PHI from patient intake forms and clinician notes. You emphasized strict logical and network separation from other tenants.
- Preference expressed: Private VPC (customer-managed control plane) but you indicated Dedicated capacity could be acceptable if we can provide customer KMS/BYOK and documented egress controls.
- Questions we promised to follow up on:
  * Can you confirm whether any data will need to reside on-prem at day 1, or is on-prem only a future option?
  * Who owns the KMS key management decisions (security or infra team)?
  * Timeline constraints from procurement (target go-live window)?

Next steps I propose (feel free to edit):
1) We prepare an "isolation proof" checklist and a short risk matrix for your security team (we can get this to you within 3 business days).
2) Align on a canary window (2–3 day pilot) where we run real traffic into a Private VPC or Dedicated slice depending on your final choice.
3) Draft a narrow SOW covering canary, KMS integration, and acceptance criteria.

Attaching a small template risk matrix + initial SOW outline in my next message. If you can answer the three bullets above it will speed things up.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

[attachment: medix_risk_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Laura Gomez <laura@medixhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment isolation needs

Hi Ben — appreciate the clear recap. Answers inline below: 

- Data classification: yes, PHI and PII. We'll need full HIPAA controls for processing and auditability.
- On-prem: not today. On-prem is a possibility in 12–18 months, but for the pilot and initial production we expect cloud hosting only.
- KMS ownership: security team owns policy; infra team will own key rotation ops. We will need BYOK support and the ability to audit key usage.
- Procurement timeline: target award by end of Q1 2027, but security review needs to see separation evidence before procurement signs.

If you can provide the checklist and a short operations playbook that shows how you enforce tenant separation and KMS integration, we can route that to our security panel this week.

Thanks —
Laura Gomez
VP Product & Digital Ops, MedixHealth
laura@medixhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: deployment isolation needs — client leaning Private but open to Dedicated

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Laura's responses. High priority: security panel wants separation evidence this week. Proposed plan:

1) Produce a 1-page ops playbook that explains how Redwood enforces logical tenant separation (namespaces, dedicated model instances, KV cache isolation, network ACLs) + KMS BYOK workflow and audit hooks.
2) Create a short risk matrix mapping Medix use-cases (PHI ingestion, model inference, logs/diagnostics) to controls and evidence.
3) Outline a 48–72 hour canary runbook we can present to their security folks — including acceptance criteria, observability checks, and rollback steps.

Can you take the ops playbook + canary runbook and a draft SOW (sow_draft_v1.pdf)? I put placeholders for costs, but we should be conservative on the Dedicated vs Private delta. Also propose owners and ETA in your reply.

Ben
Sr. Account Executive

[Forwarded message below]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: client leaning Private but open to Dedicated — ops playbook draft

Ben — I'll own the ops playbook and canary runbook. Draft plan and owners below: 

- Ops playbook (Marissa) — 1 page + appendix with diagrams (ETA: 48 hours). Will include: network segmentation diagram, namespacing details, KV cache isolation notes, audit log locations, and KMS BYOK API flow.
- Risk matrix (Karthik) — maps PHI paths and control evidence (ETA: 24 hours).
- Canary runbook (Marissa + Karthik) — steps for provisioning, traffic shaping, acceptance tests (integrity, latency, isolation), rollback criteria (ETA: 72 hours).
- Security artifacts compilation (Marissa) — SOC2 excerpt, test evidence, and audit hooks (ETA: 3 business days to pull the signed excerpts).

Notes on Dedicated vs Private:
- Private VPC (control plane customer-managed) gives Medix the clearest boundary for security sign-off but requires additional networking setup and a KMS onboarding window (~5 business days).
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed) can be provisioned faster; if we deliver BYOK + strict egress controls + separate model instances and per-tenant logs, it may meet their risk threshold for initial production.

I'll attach the first-pass risk matrix and a short SOW. Review and I'll iterate before we send to Medix.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

[attachment: sow_draft_v1.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Laura Gomez <laura@medixhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps & proposed timeline — Medix canary and evidence package

Hi Laura / Procurement — following internal work and your answers, here are the consolidated next steps and a short timeline to get security comfortable ahead of procurement: 

1) Ops playbook + risk matrix (attached) — Marissa and Karthik have prepared a 1-page playbook and a mapped risk matrix (see attachments). This shows how we enforce logical separation, KV cache isolation, per-tenant model instances, and KMS BYOK flow.
2) Evidence package — SOC2 excerpts, audit log examples, and our KMS audit hooks (we included the specific log path and retention policy).
3) Canary proposal (we can do either Private VPC or Dedicated slice):
   - Private VPC path: provisioning and KMS onboarding ~5 business days; then 2–3 day canary with your test traffic. Acceptance criteria: zero cross-tenant KV visibility, successful BYOK encrypt/decrypt operations on sample payloads, latency within agreed SLO.
   - Dedicated path: provisioning ~2 business days; BYOK + egress ACLs enabled; same canary acceptance tests.
4) Cost delta: Marissa has put conservative delta estimates in the SOW. We will refine once you pick a path.

Request: can you confirm the preferred path (Private VPC or Dedicated) and procurement target date? If helpful, here is a HubSpot link to the deal and a Drive folder with the artifacts: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8342 and https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_medix_ops_playbook

If you confirm the path, we will start provisioning a staging slice and schedule the first canary for the week of Dec 20.

Thanks and happy to hop on a quick call to walk security through the playbook.

—
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

[attachments: medix_risk_matrix.xlsx, sow_draft_v1.pdf]
